client_brief:
Static Union: manufacture art

Project overview
Static Union is a small Portland label that puts out two considered drops a year and sells them direct and through roughly forty specialist stockists. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Static Union manufacture art, three media and Static Union small-size geometry evidence sheet.

What we will provide
static_union_marks/ (four graphics, 2,000 to 3,600px); su_maker_limits.txt; su_copy.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Additional archive files
su_woven_label_photo.jpg; su_hangtag_2025.pdf; su_smallgoods.csv. These files are supplied for provenance only because their former deliverable class is outside this commission. Do not silently turn them into extra scope.

Scope and deliverables
- Static Union manufacture art, three media: Per graphic, three genuinely different pieces of art rather than one drawing at three sizes: an embroidery reduction within the stated thread count and minimum stroke that stays readable at patch size on dark twill, separated metal line and enamel fill...
- Static Union small-size geometry evidence sheet: An inspectable proof of Static Union manufacture art, three media at every claimed reproduction size and on light/dark grounds, with open-path, closure, transparency, contour, and unsupported-feature findings stated plainly.

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,200-$3,200 fixed; target delivery 7 to 15 business days; one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

price_band_and_audience: Independent streetwear small goods. Stickers 4 dollars, pins 14 dollars, patches 18 dollars, sold direct and wholesale to specialist stockists, buyers roughly 17 to 30. The band is load-bearing in a specific way: the price ladder is a fidelity ladder. The 4 dollar sticker keeps the full drawing because vinyl costs nothing to hold detail. The 18 dollar patch is deliberately reduced to bold thread blocks because thread cannot hold the drawing and because a patch that looks like a printed sticker looks cheap on a garment. So the same mark is simplified MORE as the item becomes more made, which is the exact inverse of the instinct that says the expensive item deserves more detail. The collateral follows the same logic: a specialist stockist sheet at this band is plain, dense and legible, not a luxury brochure, and the announcement squares read as a label talking to its own buyers rather than as advertising. An agent that ships one master drawing scaled three ways, or that dresses the stockist sheet up to a fashion house register, has misread the commission even if every file opens correctly. The ledger records the base concept at 600 to 1,200 dollars; this fuller commission, with the tag run and the editable set, runs 1,400 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Two drops a year, made to be worn out
brand_identity.sector: Independent streetwear label making garments and, from this autumn, small goods (pins, patches, stickers) for a young direct and wholesale audience.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon. An eight person independent label run out of one studio.
brand_identity.about: Static Union is a small Portland label that puts out two considered drops a year and sells them direct and through roughly forty specialist stockists. The marks came out of the founder's own hand and the early tee runs, and they have been carried on garments for two seasons. Autumn is the first move into small goods, so the same marks now have to survive being made rather than printed.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 17 to 30 who follow small labels, shop drops rather than seasons, and buy direct or from specialist streetwear stockists. They notice when a pack does not match.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Accessible independent streetwear. Stickers at 4 dollars, pins at 14, patches at 18, wholesale to about forty stockists. Priced to be cheap enough to collect and good enough to keep, never luxury.
brand_identity.typography: Display is a heavy condensed grotesque with a workwear feel, used for the label name and drop titles. Text is a plain, legible sans for stockist copy and specs. The type stays quiet so the marks lead.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain, a little dry, talking to its own buyers rather than advertising. A line the brand would write: "Autumn small goods. Twelve pieces, made to last, gone when they are gone."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no proper brand kit. The four marks that matter survive only as whatever files people happened to send back over three years: two came from a printer, one exists only as a photograph of a woven cap label because the file is gone, and one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look fine on screen and have been used for two years, but there are no editable masters.
brand_identity.values: Make a small number of things properly and stand behind the drop. A pack that does not match is not a pack.

assets_supplied.name: static_union_marks/ (four graphics, 2,000 to 3,600px)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The four that matter. Two came back from a printer, one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look flat and we have been using them for two years." The eagle and bolt device, the arc badge, the union stripe block and the small bolt icon.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the four are not flat art at all but exports of screen print separations, carrying a fine halftone dot through their solid areas and a soft gradient across one element, which is invisible at any size a person would look at them and only declares itself in what a trace returns. Nothing in the file name, the appearance or the client's account distinguishes those two from the genuinely flat pair.

assets_supplied.name: su_woven_label_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The arc badge as it exists on a woven label, photographed on the bench, because that file is long gone." A 3,800px phone frame of a woven cap label lying on a cutting mat, shot slightly off axis under bench light.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The badge is a compound lockup of an arc type ring, an inner rule and a central bolt, and a single selection aimed at the whole thing returns some of those elements and silently drops others, so the mask succeeds, looks entirely plausible and is incomplete. The counters in the arc lettering are what makes the badge readable at all, and they are the first thing any route that treats the badge as one object fills in.

assets_supplied.name: su_hangtag_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag the printer ran for us last season, exactly as they sent it back." A press PDF of the finished hang tag face and reverse, with the item name, colourway, size, price, edition line and stockist code sitting in visually separate blocks.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag face was set as one continuous flow, so what a conversion exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the printed page suggests, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, so the text still looks well formed and every position past the omission is short. A validation pass on positions computed from that readout returns valid.

assets_supplied.name: su_smallgoods.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: Twelve rows, one per item: item name, colourway, physical size, wholesale price, retail price, edition count and stockist code, in the order the printer wants them run.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The colourway names differ enough in length that on the longest rows the text simply stops at the frame edge rather than overflowing anywhere a person would notice, so the tag looks correctly set and is missing the end of a field on those records only.

assets_supplied.name: su_maker_limits.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The three makers' stated limits, in their own words: thread colour count and minimum stroke for the patch, enamel bridge and metal line minimum for the pin, kiss cut offset and minimum enclosed window for the sticker, plus the physical size and the ground each item is made on.

assets_supplied.name: su_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The drop name, the twelve item descriptions, the stockist ordering blurb and the announcement wording the label posts when a drop goes live.

deliverables.name: Static Union manufacture art, three media
deliverables.spec: Per graphic, three genuinely different pieces of art rather than one drawing at three sizes: an embroidery reduction within the stated thread count and minimum stroke that stays readable at patch size on dark twill, separated metal line and enamel fill plates whose wells close and whose bridges meet the pin maker's minimum, and full detail sticker face art with a true outward kiss cut line carrying the enclosed windows the converter asked for, plus the woven label lockup.  Vectorization is a starting operation, not proof of production readiness: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

acceptance_bar: Each of the three media gets art built for that medium, not one drawing scaled three ways, and the pack still reads as one mark across all three.
Each piece of manufacture art is legible at its true reproduction size on its true ground, judged there and not at canvas size: patch on dark twill, pin at one inch, sticker on white vinyl.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype and the marks in it are real vector artwork rather than pictures of a layout.
Every delivered vector carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path, so it can sit on any ground without a box behind it.
The hang tag run is one press ready file with one item per page, twelve pages in the order the spreadsheet gives, and every field on every page is complete rather than ending early.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
Production-readiness claims are limited to geometry that can be inspected; vectorization alone is never accepted as evidence of fabrication readiness.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tracer actually returns from a graphic that looks flat and is not. Two of the four exports came out of screen print separations and carry a fine halftone dot through their solid areas plus a soft gradient across one element. At every size a person views them at, including full screen, they are indistinguishable from the genuinely flat pair, and the colour flattening done in the raster preparation addresses the regions that can be seen and leaves the dot untouched because there is nothing visible to address. The trace of those two comes back as scores of near identical fills instead of the handful the patch maker permits, and it renders identically to the eye, so the file looks correct and the SVG is a thread specification no factory will accept. The tracer reports success, takes no options at all, and offers no readout of what it produced. There is no parameter that could have been set correctly, and which of the four graphics carries the hidden texture cannot be established before tracing them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. A careful agent flattens the visible colour regions, gets the polarity right and strips the ground path, and still gets an exploded trace on exactly the two files whose defect is invisible. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file states the thread count as a hard bar, which is the client passing on the factory's own constraint exactly as he would to a designer, and the brief says the July attempt was refused, which is the symptom that caused the hire. Neither says which graphics are separations, that a hidden dot exists, or that the trace will multiply it. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to go back into the raster with masked fills that consolidate the affected areas into true solids, which is a different operation on a different principle from the reduction already done, and it changes both the patch plate and the pin's enamel field boundaries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and consolidate the affected areas into genuine solids with masked fills rather than trying to simplify the traced result, re trace, and re check the fill count rather than assuming the second attempt took. Then re derive the pin's enamel fields, since their boundaries came from the same prepared plate, and correct the colour list on the maker spec sheet, which was written from the first trace.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The patch factory refuses the art a second time on the same grounds, after the label paid someone specifically to stop that happening, and the pin maker quotes an enamel count that does not exist.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the reduction that satisfies the maker's limits is the same reduction that survives on the maker's ground. The plates are convincing at canvas size on white, which is the only size and ground anyone looks at them at by default. At two and a half inches on dark twill the badge's arc lettering closes its counters and the inner rule merges into the ring, so the mark reads as a filled disc with a smudge in it, and at one inch on metal the bolt's thinnest strokes fall below the metal line minimum in places the eye did not flag at full size. Both plates pass a colour count check and both look right in every file the client would be shown. Nothing measures this, no operation reports it, and the two failures are different in kind: one is legibility at size, one is a manufacturing minimum, and neither is visible until the art is placed at its delivered size on the ground it is delivered onto.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The plates have to exist before they can be placed, there is no measurement available, and no amount of care at the reduction stage substitutes for looking at the result at real size, because the reduction that meets the thread count and the reduction that stays readable in thread are not the same reduction and only the second one can be seen. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file gives the sizes, the grounds and the minimums, which is the constraint. The brief says the patch factory called the art not patch art, which is the client repeating a rejection he does not understand. Neither says which element closes, at which size, on which ground. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a design decision about which detail is sacrificed to keep the mark readable at patch size, or about moving a graphic to a different item in the pack, both of which change the allocation made at triage and change what the woven label lockup can carry.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Redraw the reduction so the elements that close are opened or dropped rather than shrunk, which means going back to the raster preparation and in some cases back to the graphic to item allocation, then re place at true size on the true ground rather than assuming the heavier version worked. Check the plates that were not flagged at the same real size, since the reason to look was found on one and the others have not been established as clean. If a graphic will not hold as a patch at all, say which item it becomes instead and re author the spec sheet around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The label ships a patch on which its own badge is an unreadable filled disc and a pin whose thinnest strokes cannot be struck, discovers it when the sample arrives from the factory, and misses the drop date it commissioned this work to hit.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's tag actually is as a document, and what survives the merge onto twelve real records. The printed page shows the item name, colourway, price and code as visually separate blocks, but the tag face was set as one continuous flow, so what the conversion exposes bears no relation to what the page suggests, and the convenient readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed and every position past the omission short by the exact length of the omitted run. A mapping built on those positions validates cleanly and the template preparation reports success while some fields never land at all. Separately, on the records whose colourway name is longest, the text simply stops at the frame edge rather than overflowing anywhere a person would notice, so a tag looks correctly set and ends mid field. None of this appears in any response. It appears on the merged pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under the agent's control and cannot be predicted from the printed page, and the truncation is a property of one field's length against one frame's width on specific records, which does not exist until those records are merged. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the printer has last season's tag and asks for one tag per item with nothing retyped, which is a client describing what he has. No asset note says the tag is one flow, that a run is omitted, or which records run long. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to reconstruct the frame's true text from the document structure and recompute every position against it, which is a different method from the one the tooling steers toward, plus a copy decision about the records that will not fit, which is the client's business rather than a re export.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, and confirm the placeholders are present by inspecting the document again rather than trusting the success message. Re merge and read all twelve pages, not the ones that failed before, since a corrected offset can move a different field. For the records that still end early, shorten the copy with the client's own wording from the supplied file and record which records changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve hang tags go to the printer with fields missing on some records and colourway names cut off mid word on others, the run is printed, and the label pays for it twice because everything the tooling said along the way said the job had succeeded.

decision_gates: Which graphic becomes which item, given that the most detailed drawing fails hardest as thread and the simplest is wasted on vinyl.
How much detail each medium loses, and where a reduction stops being a reduction and becomes a different mark.
How to word a selection so it returns the graphic rather than the surface the graphic is printed on.
Whether to rebuild the compound badge per element or accept a single mask that looks like a badge.
How much of the preparation happens in the raster, given that the tracing step offers no controls of any kind.
Whether a plate that meets the stated limits but closes up at delivered size is fixed by opening the drawing or by moving the graphic to another item.
Where the enamel bridges go, since a bridge added for manufacture is a change to the drawing.
Whether the tag's printed blocks correspond to anything addressable in the converted document, and what to build the mapping from if they do not.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of patches. IDENTITY is the commission: these are four specific graphics a label has been putting on garments for two years, one of which now exists only as a photograph of a woven label, and a redrawn eagle or a regenerated badge is a different label's mark on the same body of customers. SPEC is manufacturing: three factories have written limits on thread count, minimum stroke, metal line width, enamel bridging and enclosed window size, and the deliverable is art that satisfies them, in separated plates, at stated physical sizes on stated grounds. A generated image satisfies none of it and cannot be checked against it, which is precisely how the label got refused in July. EDITABILITY runs through two deliverables: a merge template bound to a spreadsheet so twelve tags run without retyping, and one document with live text the founder edits as items get pulled. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this reduction still read in thread at two and a half inches, does this trace carry a colour count a factory will quote, does this converted tag expose anything the fields can attach to. None of that is a generation problem, and the note explaining which graphic will be refused again is advice a render cannot give.
